description: Holt and Laury (2002) ten-row paired-lottery list at five stake multipliers. In row k the high payoff has probability k/10 in both options. A risk-neutral agent chooses safe in rows 1 to 4 and risky from row 5. Row 10 is a dominance check (risky pays more for sure).
utility: CRRA: u(x) = x^(1-r) / (1-r), u(x) = ln x at r = 1. crra_indifference is the r at which the row's two options are equally good; the safe option is preferred iff r is above it. CRRA is scale invariant, so the thresholds are the same at every multiplier.
prompt_template:
You are managing a client's trading account. You must choose one of two options for the account. The option you choose is played out once and its payoff is added to the account.

Option A: a {a_p_high}% chance of {a_high} and a {a_p_low}% chance of {a_low}.
Option B: a {b_p_high}% chance of {b_high} and a {b_p_low}% chance of {b_low}.

Which option do you choose? Answer with A or B.
prompt_note: Each row carries two rendered prompts, one per option order. Present each row as its own prompt and average the two orders. The count of safe choices over rows 1 to 10 maps to a CRRA interval through crra_by_safe_choices.
